paragraphs.text: My dear sisters and elders, I hope you have made the most of this day. Each day the Lord gives us 24 hours with the encouragement to make the most of that time to improve ourselves.

In the Doctrine and Covenants, section 130, 18 and 19, we read, quote, whatever principle of intelligence we attain unto in this life, it will rise with us in the resurrection. And if a person gains more knowledge and intelligence in this life, through his diligence and obedience, than another, he will have so much the advantage in the world to come.
Now I'm sure you want to enter the next life with as much advantage as you can get. But how do you get it? Well, simply by using your time wisely.

During this lockdown, we have a lot of time. We can lay around and be unstructured in our approach to life. And many people do that, which is one reason so many people live a very unrewarding life. Or we can develop a plan on how to get better and how to become more capable.

As your life progresses, you are guaranteed to face a variety of circumstances, changing environments and new roles that require you to adapt to them. A personal development plan will help you to handle the pressures that come with these continuous changes and challenges so that you're well equipped to excel in all the areas of your life. This is a great time to develop that plan and to put it into action for now and after your mission.

Personal development is an ongoing process for all your life. The idea of self-improvement is not just for the mission, it's not just for education, it's not just for your career, but it's for every aspect of your life. It's about setting goals for yourself and putting plans into place to reach those goals.
Here are four specific reasons why personal development should be a priority in your life.

Number one, it forces you out of your comfort zone. If there are areas of your life that you don't like or which are not good or you're not good at them, those are the weaknesses that a personal development plan can help you improve on. Confronting these areas and improving on them can help to push you out of the comfort zone, building your comfort zone into a bigger zone and this allows you to experience growth and improve your skills and that builds on itself causing you to keep building out and out and out until literally you're comfortable doing anything.

Number two, it develops your strengths. A personal development plan not only helps you improve on your weaknesses, but it can also help you develop your strengths by taking time to focus on nurturing and using your strengths more, you go from being good at something to being great at it. You can reach your potential and achieve great growth by developing the skills you're already good at.

Number three, it boosts your confidence. Making the decision to improve on your skills takes you a step closer to feeling more confident. Once you've achieved a certain goal, gaining another skill or developing a certain area of your life, you naturally feel good about yourself. The more you keep on developing in the areas of your life you are not confident at present, the more you can boost your confidence.

Number four, it improves your self-awareness. Personal development is closely linked to self-awareness. It gives you the opportunity to take an honest look at the areas of your life that need improvement. Through this process, you get to know who you really are, what your true values are, and where you would like to go in life. Once you go through this process, you will improve your self-awareness and your experience fulfillment. Life will just be more satisfying to you.
Now, when you embark on the journey of personal development, keep these six steps in mind.
Number one, establish the goals you want to reach in all areas of your life. Be comprehensive. That'd be a good project for you tonight and tomorrow.
Number two, look for the weaknesses that need improvement in order for you to reach these goals. Be honest with yourself about that.
Number three, identify the different opportunities that you have to develop the weaknesses into strengths.
Next, set up your plan of action for improving those weaknesses.
Next, make time for nurturing your strengths. Actually set aside time in your schedule. From 9 to 10, I'm going to work on this strength. Or from 1 to 2, I'm going to work on that strength.

And finally, record the outcomes of your development. Measure yourself. Evaluate your outcomes against your goal. So get yourself in a mindset like an Olympic athlete, where you're tracking your performance and measuring it against where you need to be to win that gold medal.

The journey of self-improvement is an ongoing process, literally, of constantly learning. I love learning and it's blessed my life so much, I cannot talk more highly about it. It's just incredible to get addicted to learning. It gives you the opportunity to constantly push your strengths into higher levels and make your weaknesses become irrelevant.

Remember, personal development can help you in all the areas of your life. It's therefore a personal journey, but it's your journey and one that needs to be prioritized because if you don't do it, no one else is going to do it for you. The benefits are simple that you will grow as a person while you grow your skills. You improve your self-awareness while you build and boost your self-confidence.

Elders and sisters, what you choose to do will be up to you. And the follow-through will also be up to you. You can make these days in quarantine some of the most productive, powerful days of your life or you can let them be some of the most boring and useless days of your life. The choice is yours, but the consequences are yours too. With our God-given gift of agency, we are each given the blessing of being able to choose what we will do with our time and our energy, but and this is important, we don't get to choose the consequences. The consequences are eternally bonded to our choices. When you make a certain choice, you automatically choose a certain consequence. So use your time well.
Here are some things I would suggest you consider.

Number one, study English. Video record yourself doing each lesson in English. Record yourself reading out loud. The Book of Mormon in English, send short video clips of yourself teaching in English to Sister Hughes and she will help you get better.

Number two, exercise your body. Do two sessions of 30 minutes of exercise each day except on Sundays. See how many push-ups or sit-ups you can build up to or do planks and see how long you can hold the plank. Do yoga, which is one of my favorite exercises because it works with the mind and the body. Help a good 30-minute routine and do it every day.

Three, set a daily goal for how many video chats you can do with members of your assigned wards. Ask the members questions about their life and then become a good listener. Each of these members would love to talk about their life to someone who is really an attentive listener. It would help them forget about some of the problems they're facing right now and the fears that they have on their mind.
Number four, memorize the 30 Dale Carnegie human relations principles and see how many you can use in a single day.
Five, memorize the 42 doctrinal points and then memorize the scriptures that support them from the Book of Mormon.

These are just a few of the thousands of appropriate choices you can make. I plead with you to turn these quarantine days into a personal university of self-development. The most important years of your life are still ahead of you, so get prepared to live them well.
I love you elders and sisters. Let's go forward in faith.
